categories.name: Fast Triage / Minimal Evaluation
categories.description: Short, rapid patient encounters concluding quickly after initial triage and minimal lab work without progression to admission or intensive treatment.
categories.rationale: Characterized by very low duration (minutes), short trace lengths, and outcomes like ER Sepsis Triage or basic lab tests.

categories.name: Standard Acute Care & Treatment
categories.description: Standard emergency department pathways involving comprehensive diagnostics (blood tests) followed by acute interventions such as IV liquids and IV antibiotics.
categories.rationale: Medium duration (hours to a few days) with intermediate trace lengths, ending in IV antibiotics or initial admission/release.

categories.name: Inpatient Admission & Controlled Release
categories.description: Encounters requiring inpatient nursing or intensive care unit admission following diagnostics and treatment, eventually resulting in a stable release.
categories.rationale: Longer durations (days) involving bed allocation (Admission NC/IC) and structured discharge outcomes (Release A, B, C, D).

categories.name: Chronic Readmission & Heavy Rework
categories.description: Extremely long, highly complex pathways characterized by extensive repetition of lab tests and admissions, frequently resulting in patient return to the emergency room.
categories.rationale: Extreme duration (up to hundreds of days), massive trace lengths, heavy rework observed across multiple variables, and Return ER outcomes.
